title: Great Oxidation Event
summary: About 2.4 billion years ago, oxygen from cyanobacteria began to build up in Earth's atmosphere once dissolved iron in the oceans, which had been absorbing it, was used up. The change allowed an ozone layer to form and helped trigger the first ice age, though its exact timing and speed remain debated.

uncertainty.note: NASA gives about 2.4 billion years ago; Kaufman and colleagues (via Science News) place the event at about 2.316 billion years ago from sulfur isotopes. Both sources say timing and abruptness are debated.

where.modern_name: Global atmosphere and oceans (no single location)

importance.justification: Permanently changed the atmosphere and oceans, enabling oxygen-using life and reshaping the chemistry of the planet.

sources.title: Oxygen levels on early Earth rose and fell several times before the successful Great Oxidation Event
